title.narrative: Access of vulnerable populations to decent and productive work, and value of public goods are increased through Employment Intensive Investment Programmes

description.narrative: The construction sector in Lebanon is a powerful motor for employment, development, and shared prosperity in a region wracked by the impact of conflicts. Adapting new approaches in the construction sector will ensure more inclusion and job employment opportunities, as well as more construction skills within the community. Infrastructure projects not only foster economic growth but also act as catalysts for the creation of decent work. By generating a range of jobs during the construction, operation, and maintenance phases, infrastructure development directly contributes to reducing unemployment and underemployment. ILO is adopting the Employment Intensive Infrastructure Programme (EIIP) approach aiming to link infrastructure development with short-term employment creation, poverty reduction and local economic and social development. In using local labour and resources, they create much-needed employment and income, reduce costs, and support local industry while increasing the capacity of local institutions. The core strategy of the EIIP approach including Local Resource-Based Technology (LRBT) and Decent Work Principles (DWP) is to rehabilitate and maintain public infrastructure and Green Works, complemented by training for contractors and implementing partners and capacity building within public institutions providing them with the needed tools to ensure low-cost sustainability of projects beyond the EIIP, in addition to short-term job creation enabling vulnerable communities and social protection beneficiaries to quickly earn cash in public projects such as road repair and infrastructure rehabilitation. In achieving this, attention will be given to the establishment of sustainable and resilient livelihood practices which is in line with the UNSDCF Outcome 1 on Prosperity with the objectives to “boost productive sectors” and “improve the business environment” to generate new, equal and inclusive income opportunities.
